server.instructions:
GoMMO Studio is one window over a game client (or an MMO World folder) and a project, and the user watches every call you make happen in it. Its tools are grouped by prefix: studio_ for the window (what is open, showing a document or panel, a screenshot of everything, a photo of the map or model in front at any size, saving the project under a name), map_ for the map editor, model_ for the model viewer, packs_ for browsing and extracting the client's archives, texture_ for editing the open model's textures (recolor, paint, fill, resize, format, mips, undo; one call is one undo step), and server_ for running the project's linked game server (server_test_in_game installs, restarts the server when needed and launches the client; server_check_in_client also runs the real client unattended through a check list and returns its pictures beside Studio's; server_verify_run plans a check for every change of the review on RF, runs them in one client session and scores each picture against Studio's as pass, needs a look or failed to reach, kept per project for server_verify_results; server_simulate_start runs headless bots on throwaway copies of the server, with and without the project's edits, and server_simulate_compare says what the edits changed; gamedata_balance_targets, gamedata_balance_run and gamedata_balance_apply turn levelling and economy targets into reviewed game data changes), project_ for reviewing and reverting everything Install would write (map_install, map_plan_install, project_changes and server_test_in_game take a scope: item for the map or document in focus, project for everything; map_plan_install and map_install also take only or exclude, a list of the change keys project_changes returns), script_ for the server's Lua scripts, dialog_ for NPC dialog text, gamedata_ for the server's game data tables (items, monsters, skills, stores), edited as a project copy (model_rows lists the rows that draw a model), and asset_ for what reads each client file and what a model reads; sound_ lists, plays, replaces, trims, fades and normalizes the client's sounds and saves them into the project (one sound_edit call is one undo step); ui_ edits the client's interface (its windows and controls: move, resize, re-anchor, re-art; one call is one undo step; ui_render draws a window as the client places it, and controls the client's code binds to are never deleted or renamed), and sprite_ exports, replaces and adds the pages of RF Online's .spr sheets; effect_ opens, plays, edits and saves World of Kung Fu effect files (.sfx: elements, keys and materials by parameter name; one effect_set call is one undo step); compare_ diffs the open client against another client folder of the same game and takes its files into the project; project_check runs every check over the project before Install in one report; project_export_package and project_import_package share a whole project as one .zip with another Studio user, and project_publish puts the project's client changes into the linked server's client folder and launcher manifest, so players' launchers download them; studio_history lists every open document's undo steps and studio_history_goto goes to one; studio_palette_search finds anything the command palette offers and studio_palette_run runs it; studio_widgets and studio_input drive the window itself, clicking its controls by label as a user would. Start with studio_status. Open a client with map_open_client or a project with map_open_project; the model viewer, packs and textures all follow that client. studio_report_bug files a bug about Studio to its team when the user has signed in to their oldschoolops.com account (studio_account says whether); signing in is optional and only the user can do it. Edits go into the project, never straight into the client: map_install writes the project's maps and files into the client and server, backing up what it replaces. A call that cannot run says why and which tool to call first. macro_ records the edits you make and replays them. live_ reaches the running RF or WoKF server through the Studio link (the welcome lists what each answers): its status, log, players and monsters on a map, GM commands, spawns, Play from here and the real kills and drops, and the other Studios on that server with the documents they hold (live_peers, live_locks) and the changes they saved (live_changes, live_change_reload, live_change_dismiss) and the table and map edits co-edited with them as they happen (live_coedit_status, live_coedit_recent, live_coedit_conflicts, live_coedit_resolve, live_lock_doc, live_unlock_doc), plus what the server observes: heat grids per map (live_heat; map_live_heat_overlay shows, hides and sets them on the open map's ground), recordings to replay on the map (live_record_start, live_record_replay; map_live_replay plays, pauses, seeks and sets the speed), the money and item economy per currency with the value of each monster's drops (live_economy), and live monster edits that live_monster_save stages as game data, and the Lua script debugger (live_script_break sets breakpoints kept with the project, live_script_hits and live_script_hit read stacks and locals, live_script_eval and live_script_continue drive a paused script; script_debug_watch keeps watch expressions); checkpoint_ makes, compares and restores named snapshots of the whole project; project_branches lists the project's branches (named lines of work, each its own copy of the maps, files and game data), project_branch_create, project_branch_switch, project_branch_rename and project_branch_delete manage them, project_branch_diff compares two by game data cell, map object and file, and project_branch_merge three-way merges one into the live one with a conflict per cell, object or file;blender_ is the live link to Blender's GoMMO Bridge add-on (blender_bridge_install puts the add-on into Blender, blender_bridge_status, blender_push, blender_pull, blender_bridge_stop), streaming the model in front and its edits both ways with the RF constraint report. RF designers: skill_design_ opens and edits a skill or force with its effects and balance read; loc_ is the Localization workspace (strings, translation proposals and review, glossary, the bundle language); craft_ is the recipe designer (recipe trees, material sources, value verdicts, create and edit); cashshop_ is the cash shop designer (catalogue, prices, pricing review, sales scheduled through Live ops). model_mesh_view switches the model viewer's Edit tab between its modes and views, and model_mesh_limits measures the edit session against the game family's limits (vertices, weights, bones, texture sizes). studio_assistant_status reports the built-in Assistant panel (key set or not, model, a job waiting for the user's review) and studio_assistant_model picks its model; studio_assistant_recipes, studio_assistant_recipe_save and studio_assistant_recipe_delete manage its saved requests and studio_assistant_budget its cost guard; only the user sends it requests, runs recipes and queues, and answers its confirmations.

Map editor: The map editor is a world editor for MMOs: it places and edits the props, monster spawns, NPCs, portals, regions, paths, walls and grids of a world's maps. Call map_status first. Open an MMO World folder or a game client (map_open_client), a project folder (map_open_project), or make a new world (map_new_world), then a map (map_list_maps, map_open_map; map_new_map adds one to a world). Positions are the editor's render-space units with z up (an MMO World's own units); omit z when adding and the object lands on the ground. Every edit is one undo step and stays in the editor until map_save_project writes it: an MMO World saves straight into its folder, a game client into the project folder. For a game client, map_install writes into the client and server, backing up every file it replaces; map_restore_backup puts them back. MMO World, DragonSoul, World of Kung Fu and RF maps have an editable terrain (map_terrain_info says what reaches the game, map_terrain_new then map_terrain_sculpt). Grouped objects (map_group_objects) select as one; a listed object's group field names its group. map_walk_start walks the open map as the game's character where the game supports it. Call map_screenshot to see the result.

Model viewer: The model viewer shows a game client's models: characters, creatures and items, with their animations, dress-up, attached effects and (in RF) force and skill effects. Call model_status first; once a client is open, find models with model_search and open one with model_open. Change what is shown with model_animation, model_dress, model_view_options and model_camera, and call model_screenshot to see it. model_capture and model_export_gltf write files to the user's capture folder; model_extract_files copies the open model's files into the project, where edits hot-reload. model_clip_trim, model_clip_retime, model_clip_reverse, model_clip_splice, model_clip_loop, model_clip_key and model_clip_edit edit the current clip, and model_clip_export writes it. model_gallery_preview and model_gallery_run picture every model of a category, group, search or key list into a folder with an index; model_gallery_status and model_gallery_cancel follow it. In RF, model_list_effects and model_effect_set edit the attached effects and the spell picked in the Spells tab or by model_play_spell live, and model_effect_save writes them into the project.

tools.description: What the window shows: the client, the project, every open document with the pane it is in, the focused one, the split view, the left panel and the panels studio_show can switch to.
tools.name: studio_status

tools.description: Bring a document to the front, show two documents side by side, show a left panel, open or fold the map's problems dock, or open or close the Install dialog. Several maps and models can be open at once; the map_ and model_ tools act on the map and the model in front. Every argument is optional; returns studio_status.

beside.description: An open document from studio_status documents to show beside the one in front, splitting the view

dock.description: Open (true) or fold (false) the problems and changes dock under the map

document.description: A map, a model, or an MMO World's world graph; with name, which kind name means

focus.description: Give the left or right pane of a split view the keyboard, the inspector and the tools

install.description: Open (true) or close (false) the Install dialog, which only plans until its Install button is pressed

left_panel.description: Show (true) or hide (false) the left panel; panel also shows it

macros.description: Open (true) or close (false) the Macros dialog (needs a client open)

name.description: Which open document to bring to the front: a name, map key or model key from studio_status documents (default: the last of that kind)

panel.description: A name from studio_status panels: maps, models, packs, server, scripts, game data, where used, or one of the open map's panels such as Layers, Spawns or Lights

photo.description: Enter (true) or leave (false) photo mode, where the map or model in front fills the window at the photo's shape; studio_photo takes the picture

review.description: Open (true) or close (false) the changes review: everything Install would write, with diffs and Revert

split.description: Split the view (true) with the next open document beside the one in front, or close the split (false)

tools.name: studio_show

tools.description: A picture of the whole window as the user sees it, once loading has settled, with studio_status beside it.

save.description: Also save the full-size picture to this absolute .png path (an existing file must be a PNG)

tools.name: studio_screenshot

tools.description: Render the map or model in front from its current camera at any size up to 8192 pixels a side, whatever the window's size, without gizmos, labels, grid or interface, and save it as a PNG; returns a preview. Aim the camera first (map_camera, model tools).

max_size.description: Longest edge of the returned preview (default 1600)

save.description: Absolute .png path (default: a new file in the Photos folder under Pictures)

supersample.description: Draw at twice the size and scale down for smoother edges (default true; skipped past 4096 a side)

transparent.description: A model's background left transparent (models only)

tools.name: studio_photo

tools.description: Cross the map and the model: open the selected spawn's monster as a model, or start placing the open model on the map, where the user clicks to drop it.

action.description: spawn_model needs one spawn selected (map_select); place_model needs a map and any model open, and bakes a model the game's maps cannot name into a prop first

tools.name: studio_link

tools.description: Copy the project, an unsaved scratch one included, to a new named project in the projects folder and switch to it.

name.description: The new project's name, which also names its folder

tools.name: studio_save_project_as

tools.description: Walk the open map as the game's character: collision, game camera height and the map's fog, until map_walk_stop puts the editor camera back where it was.

at.description: [x, y] stands on the ground there, [x, y, z] on the floor nearest that height

first_person.description: Look from the character's eyes instead of the chase camera

tools.name: map_walk_start

tools.description: Stop walking and put the editor camera back exactly where it was.
tools.name: map_walk_stop

tools.description: Stand the walking character somewhere else on the map.

at.description: [x, y] stands on the ground there, [x, y, z] on the floor nearest that height

tools.name: map_walk_teleport

tools.description: Walk the character for some seconds, relative to where the camera faces, then report where it got to; seconds 0 only changes the view.

distance.description: Chase camera distance in world units, clamped to 0.3x-4x the game's

first_person.description: Switch to the character's eyes (true) or the chase camera (false)

jump.description: Jump at the start, where the game has a jump

pitch.description: Tilt the camera to this many degrees first, -80 to 85; positive looks down

run.description: Run (true) or walk (false), kept as the gait like the run key; omitted, the current gait

seconds.description: How long to walk, up to 30 (default 1)

yaw.description: Turn the camera to this heading in degrees first

tools.name: map_walk_move

tools.description: Whether the map is being walked, where the character stands, the camera, the nearest live players and monsters drawn, and the game's walking numbers with the ones not derived from the game marked unverified.
tools.name: map_walk_status

tools.description: Play in Studio: log Studio's GM test character in on the linked server at a spot on the open map, walking and fighting with the game's own session, until map_play_stop logs it out.

at.description: [x, y] in the editor's world, or [x, y, z]; omitted, the camera's spot

character.description: Name for a new test character; the test account's existing character is used when it has one

race.description: The game's race number for a new character (RF: race-sex code 0-4)

tools.name: map_play_start

tools.description: Log the Play character out and put the editor camera back.
tools.name: map_play_stop

tools.description: Move the Play character for some seconds relative to the camera, sending the game's own movement messages, then report where it got to.

run.description: Run (true) or walk (false); omitted, the current gait

seconds.description: How long to move, up to 30 (default 1)

yaw.description: Turn the camera to this heading in degrees first

tools.name: map_play_move

tools.description: Walk the Play character to a point or an entity and wait until it arrives, is stopped, or a minute passes.

at.description: [x, y] or [x, y, z] in the editor's world

id.description: Entity id from map_play_status nearby; omitted, at is required

tools.name: map_play_goto

tools.description: Target an entity, as a click on it does; with no id the nearest monster, with id 0 clear the target.

id.description: Entity id from map_play_status nearby; omitted, the nearest monster

tools.name: map_play_target

tools.description: Attack an entity, walking into reach and swinging until it dies, the character moves, or seconds pass; reports the fight.

id.description: Entity id from map_play_status nearby; omitted, the target, else the nearest monster

seconds.description: Stop waiting after this long, up to 60 (default 20); the fight carries on

tools.name: map_play_attack

tools.description: Walk to a ground item and pick it up; with no id the nearest.

id.description: Entity id from map_play_status nearby; omitted, the nearest ground item

tools.name: map_play_loot

tools.description: Talk to an NPC: open its dialog with the text and numbered choices (an RF NPC's dialog is its store); with no id the target or the nearest NPC.

id.description: Entity id from map_play_status nearby; omitted, the target, else the nearest NPC

tools.name: map_play_talk

tools.description: Pick a choice in the open NPC dialog (for a store, buy that item).

choice.description: Choice number from map_play_talk, counted from 1

tools.name: map_play_choose

tools.description: Say something in the game's local chat as the Play character.
tools.name: map_play_chat

tools.description: Run one of the game's GM commands as the Play character, such as level 30, heal or a monster call.

command.description: The command without its prefix, as typed in game

tools.name: map_play_gm

tools.description: Whether Play is on, and the character's HP, FP, SP, level, experience, map, position, target, open dialog, inventory, equipment, money, nearest entities and the latest chat and fight lines.
tools.name: map_play_status

tools.description: Show, hide or set the heat grid the viewport lays on the ground from the linked server's insight.heat, then report it; with no arguments it only reports.

kind.description: deaths, kills, move (position samples) or dwell (seconds spent per cell)

opacity.description: How strongly the grid is drawn, 0.1 to 1

panel.description: Open or close the Heat map panel in the viewport

scale.description: Cell size as a multiple of the server's base cell: 1, 2, 4 or 8

show.description: Draw the heat grid on the ground

tools.name: map_live_heat_overlay

tools.description: Drive the replay bar of the recording open on this map (live_record_replay opens and closes one): play, pause, seek, speed, trails, or stop just before an event; with no arguments it only reports.

at.description: Move the playhead to this many seconds into the recording

event.description: Pause 2 s before this event, by its index in events

events.description: Include every event held so far, with its index

play.description: Play (true, from the start when at the end) or pause (false)

trails.description: No trails, player trails, or every entity's trail

tools.name: map_live_replay

tools.description: The live world overlay as it stands: the running server's players and monsters on the open map, through Studio's link, in server and editor coordinates.
tools.name: map_live_entities

tools.description: What the editor has open: client, project, map, selection, unsaved edits, camera, and recent client and project folders.
tools.name: map_status

tools.description: Open an MMO World folder or a game client's install folder. Saves and closes whatever is open first.

path.description: The world folder or the client's install folder

tools.name: map_open_client

tools.description: Create a new MMO World in an empty or missing folder, with the default object kinds and one blank map, and open it.

name.description: The world's name; the folder's name when left out

path.description: An absolute folder that is empty or does not exist yet

tools.name: map_new_world

tools.description: Run the open MMO World's Lua exporters against its saved maps, writing each one's files into its output folder. Save first to export unsaved edits.

name.description: One exporter's name from world.json; every exporter when left out

tools.name: map_run_exporters

tools.description: Export the open game client map into an MMO World: its objects with the game's own kinds and fields, its geometry as terrain, its prop models and its monsters. The client is not changed.

path.description: An absolute MMO World folder, or an empty or missing folder for a new world

tools.name: map_export_world

tools.description: Generate the open MMO World map's walkable grid (named walk: 0 walkable, 1 blocked) from its geometry, as one undo step.
tools.name: map_generate_walkable

tools.description: Build the open map's editable terrain from a greyscale image, as one undo step (map_terrain_new with source image does the same). path.description: An absolute PNG or JPEG file

tools.name: map_import_heightmap

tools.description: Add a blank map to the open MMO World and open it in a tab of its own. On a DragonSoul client: a flat map of size tiles a side (folder of tiles, config.xml, grids, region names), which Install writes into the client and, with the server linked, into its maps folder and mapconfig.xml.

path.description: The project folder

tools.name: map_open_project

query.description: Words to match

tools.name: map_open_map

tools.description: The open map's settings, object kinds (with their fields and what can be added), layers, grids and bounds.

offset.description: Skip this many matches, for the next page

radius.description: With near: only objects within this distance

side.description: Objects the client files hold, or the linked server's

ids.description: Object ids, as map_list_objects returns them

tools.name: map_get_objects

frame.description: Point the camera at the selection

ids.description: Object ids, as map_list_objects returns them; an empty list clears the selection

kind.description: Select every object of this kind instead of ids

mode.description: How the new objects join the selection (default replace)

name.description: The object's name in the editor

radius.description: A round object's radius, such as a spawn's area

size.description: A box's half extents [x, y, z]

A weapon or shield binds to the open model's skeleton; armour and cloaks write one mesh per body the cloned row fits, each bound to that body's skeleton. It takes a free mesh number and model code, adds a resource.dat record per mesh (Player Mesh for armour, Item Mesh otherwise), clones the item row with a new item code and names it in the locale tables, all into the project's files, then lists the item in the model browser. rf15: a COSTUMEARMOR like (e.g. BELMALE_COSTUMEARMOR_UPPER_012.MSH) makes a costume item, queued in cupperitem ... ccloakitem. dt.description: move: seconds to shift the keys by

tools.description: Search the table of player-visible strings; each row has its text in every language, where it lives, its byte limit and codepage, and any fit problem.

kind.description: item, monster, npc, skill, quest, npc dialog, ui, ... (loc_status lists them)

lang.description: Language code from loc_status (en, zh-TW, pt-BR or a user-added one)

query.description: Words every listed string holds, in any language, its id or code

state.description: Only cells of lang in this state

unfit.description: Only cells of lang that do not fit their field

tools.name: loc_strings

tools.description: The next cells of a language that need a translation and have no draft queued: the source text, the field's byte limit in its codepage (a CJK character is 2 bytes in Big5, GBK, CP949 and Shift-JIS; a letter is 1 in a Windows codepage), and the glossary wording each must use.

copies.description: Also cells that hold the source text unchanged

unfit.description: Also cells, and queued drafts, too long for their field, to shorten

tools.name: loc_untranslated

tools.description: Put translations in the review queue, marked with their origin; each is checked against its field's byte limit and the glossary. Nothing reaches the game data until loc_review_decide accepts it.

drafts.description: [{id, text}] (a lang per draft overrides lang)

lang.description: Language code from loc_status (en, zh-TW, pt-BR or a user-added one)

note.description: A note the reviewer sees beside each proposal

tools.name: loc_propose

tools.description: The review queue: each draft's id (lang|row), text, origin, source and whether it can be accepted.

lang.description: Language code from loc_status (en, zh-TW, pt-BR or a user-added one)

limit.description: At most this many drafts (default all)

tools.name: loc_review

tools.description: Accept or reject queued drafts. Accepted ones are written as one undo step (game data cells through the normal pending edits, the rest into the project's localization file) and saved.

accept.description: true writes them, false drops them

all.description: Every queued draft instead of ids

force.description: Accept drafts that break the glossary (never ones that do not fit)

ids.description: Draft ids from loc_review

save.description: Save the game data after accepting (default true)

tools.name: loc_review_decide

tools.description: Write one cell now, refused when the text does not fit its field; save the game data afterwards to keep a game data cell.

id.description: The string's id from loc_strings

lang.description: The language the text is in

tools.name: loc_set

tools.description: Add a language column to the project.

code.description: A code such as de or es

name.description: The language's display name

script.description: The writing system, so Studio can tell whether a client can show it

tools.name: loc_language_add

tools.description: Add, change or remove a glossary term: every translation of a string whose source holds the term must use its wording.

note.description: Guidance translators see beside the term

tools.name: loc_glossary_set

tools.description: Check the table: cells that break the glossary, and cells that do not fit their field, per language.

lang.description: Language code from loc_status (en, zh-TW, pt-BR or a user-added one)

tools.name: loc_check

tools.description: Translation memory: queue, for review, the translation already given to the same source text for every missing cell of a language.

lang.description: The language to fill from translation memory

tools.name: loc_memory_fill

tools.description: Make a bundle's language: write the language's text into the client folder and server column the client shows, as one undo step, keeping that folder's own text in the project's localization file, and save. folder.description: The client folder to write it into (default the one the shipped client loads)

code.description: The template's code; blank for the first skill

kind.description: monster makes the design a monster skill

tools.description: The effect and requirement vocabulary of the open game's own rows: instant effects with names, lasting stat indices by param code, area shapes, classes, grades and mastery lines per table, and the races pattern.
tools.name: skill_design_effects

tools.description: Run the design's content checks (missing client row, text too long for its field, effect code unknown, requirement impossible) and plan its save without writing anything: the server row, the client record with the columns this client keeps unverified, the cast clips and effect ids, and a monster skill's AI row.
tools.name: skill_design_check

tools.description: Create the open design: the server row and the client record together as ONE game data save (Undo last save or gamedata_create_undo takes it all back), journaled with the project, read back by the server's own loaders. Refused while a check finds a problem.

tools.description: Where the design lands with Auto-balance's model: damage a cast, casts and seconds a kill, damage per FP against the target player level's monsters, compared with the existing attacking skills of its class and grade, and a kill-time curve around the target level.

item.description: An item code: the document opens on its recipes and recipe tree

tools.name: craft_open

tools.description: Every recipe of the open RF game data: itemmakedata (crafting with a make tool, 07/0F), itemcombine (the talic exchange, 07/1C) and combinetable/combinetable2 (combine), with each one's manual index (what the client asks by), products, materials, fee, races mask, combine chance and event gating; and what the tables of this version lack.

filter.description: Only recipes whose id, code, product or material codes or names hold every one of these words

item.description: Only recipes that make this item

kind.description: Only crafting (make), combine or item combine (exchange) recipes

tools.name: craft_list

tools.description: One recipe whole: its row, products and materials with their names, why no player can run it if none can, the value read (craft_value), and the client's own record of it: what the client shows, where it differs from the server, and which of its columns Studio may write on this version.

recipe.description: The recipe's id, table#row (craft_list lists them)

tools.name: craft_get

tools.description: An item's recipe tree: down to raw materials through the first live recipe of each crafted item (with how many of each one item takes, where each comes from: monster loot, store, quest reward, cash shop, box, another recipe; flagging unobtainable materials, codes no table holds and cycles), and the reverse, every recipe that uses the item.
tools.name: craft_tree

tools.description: The recipe cost and value model: the fee plus each material at its cheapest (a store's price, another recipe's cost, or farm time from Auto-balance's kill model and drop rates priced at that monster's money per hour, else the list price) against the expected product (list and sell price, chance, count, and the product's power against the gear a player of its level wears); a verdict of underpriced (product worth 1.5x the cost or more), overpriced (0.67x or less), fair, dead (no player can run it) or unknown; and the money one craft moves: the fee into the server's craft sink, store money spent, and the sell-back. Without a recipe, the verdict counts and the recipes with the chosen verdict.

filter.description: Only recipes whose codes or names hold every one of these words

kind.description: Only crafting (make), combine or item combine (exchange) recipes

recipe.description: One recipe; omit for a summary of many

tools.name: craft_value

tools.description: Make a new recipe for an item as a game data edit: a row appended to the kind's table with the next manual index (combine recipes go into combinetable2, whose indexes follow the first table's fixed count), saved as one undoable game data save that travels through branches, .gommomod, co-editing and Install like any edit, then read back by the version's own recipe loader and taken back if refused. civil.description: The m_strCivil races mask, 0 or 1 per race and sex, such as 11111

dry_run.description: Only check and plan; nothing is saved

fee.description: Dalant the server charges (combine m_dwCommit, item combine m_dwFee; a make-tool craft charges none)

like.description: A recipe id whose other columns the new row copies (default the first live recipe of the table)

outputs.description: The whole output list (crafting and combine recipes): [{code: item code (or an LR result group on a combine recipe), weight: out of 10000, count: combine only}] in slot order

civil.description: The m_strCivil races mask, 0 or 1 per race and sex, such as 11111

dry_run.description: Only check and plan; nothing is saved

fee.description: Dalant the server charges (combine m_dwCommit, item combine m_dwFee; a make-tool craft charges none)

tools.description: Switch a recipe off in place, as one undoable game data save: a combine row's m_bCombineExist 0, a crafting row's output weights 0, an item combine row's code -1. Rows are not deleted, because a deletion renumbers every later manual index the client asks by.

dry_run.description: Only check and plan; nothing is saved

recipe.description: The recipe's id, table#row (craft_list lists them)

tools.name: craft_delete

tools.description: Check every recipe: a product no item table holds, a material no table holds or no source a player can reach gives, a product whose list price is under its materials', a manual index two rows share, a row whose index is not its row or past what the request can carry (or a combinetable row past the version's first-table count), Golden Box recipes this server never runs, and cycles. The project's recipes are compared with the unmodified server data, so only what the project introduced is a finding; what was already so is counted as retail.

limit.description: At most this many findings per list (default 200)

retail.description: Also list the findings already in the unmodified data

tools.description: The open RF game data's cash shop (rf2232, rf415, rf455): the server's nation and price column, which client files are written, and every row with its item, tab, price, badges, timer, running or scheduled sale and any disagreement with the client's own catalogue.

filter.description: Only rows whose item code or name holds this

hidden.description: Include the rows the client does not list

show.description: Also open the Cash shop document

tab.description: Only one tab, by number (1-14, 0 featured) or name

store.description: The row's store index (m_dwIndex, the client's StoreIdx)

tools.name: cashshop_get

tools.description: Edit the cash shop as staged game data (one undo step, journaled, carried by branches, .gommomod, co-editing and Install): reprice a row or many by a percentage, set per-nation prices, show or hide, set the discount, badges or item, move it within its tab, or change a timed item's duration. badges.description: The row's badges: any of New, Best, Hit, GM, Limited; [] clears them

discount.description: m_nCsDiscount; the client compares its own byte with it on every buy

item.description: Point the row at another item code

move.description: Swap the row with the listed row before or after it in its tab

nation.description: The nation code price sets (KR, GB, TW...); the version's cash shop price table must have its column

seconds.description: A timed item's duration (its timeritem row, which every grant of the item follows)

store.description: The row's store index (m_dwIndex, the client's StoreIdx)

tab.description: percent: every listed row of this tab

timer.description: Count a timed item's duration in play time or real time

visible.description: Show (true) or hide (false) the row; a hidden row keeps its design

tools.name: cashshop_edit

tools.description: List an item in the cash shop: it takes over a freed row (one Remove left), else the last hidden row past the featured ones, since neither the server's catalogue nor the client's files take a new row. Marks the item a cash item when it is not, which the client's list requires.

badges.description: Any of New, Best, Hit, GM, Limited

tools.name: cashshop_add

hide_only.description: Hide the row and keep its prices, instead of freeing it for Add

store.description: The row's store index (m_dwIndex, the client's StoreIdx)

tools.name: cashshop_remove

tools.description: Review every listed row's price: against its category's curve (price per gold value), the best earnable gear at its level band (pay-to-win), duplicates, and the hours of play its gold value takes; each row gets a suggested price and the reasoning.

economy.description: Build the Economy designer's money model first, so prices are set against gold earned per hour

flagged.description: Only the rows with a flag

tools.name: cashshop_price_check

discount.description: Percent off, 1-90, for every row without its own

id.description: Replace this sale event

items.description: Rows with their own terms: [{store, discount?, limit?}]; limit caps the units one run sells (the client's limited sale)

name.description: The event's name on the Live ops calendar

tools.name: cashshop_schedule_sale

tools.description: The storefront as the client lays it out: the three featured slots (rows 0-8), then every tab in order with its listed rows, prices, badges and sales.

tools.description: Propose spawn changes from the linked server's heat: each server spawn on the map gets the kills and player deaths of the heat cells nearest it, per hour since the heat was reset; over-farmed camps get a faster respawn or more monsters, death traps fewer and slower ones, empty and quiet camps are flagged and left alone. Writes nothing; live_spawn_tune_apply writes the accepted proposals.

aim.description: The share of capacity a tuned over-farmed camp aims for (default 0.6)

busy.description: Kills per hour over this share of a camp's capacity (count × 3600 / respawn) is over-farmed (default 0.8)

death_share.description: ...and deaths per kill at or over this (default 0.25)

deaths_per_hour.description: Player deaths per hour at a camp before it can be a death trap (default 6)

map.description: Map key or title to open first; the map in front when left out

max_grow.description: The most a proposal multiplies a camp's count or respawn speed by (default 2)

min_hours.description: The least heat history to propose from (default 0.5)

min_respawn.description: The fastest respawn in seconds a proposal writes (default 5)

prefer.description: An over-farmed camp gets a faster respawn first (default) or more monsters first

quiet.description: Under this share a camp is flagged quiet and left alone (default 0.05)

all.description: Every proposed change instead of ids

ids.description: Spawn ids from live_spawn_tune_propose

tools.description: Write the accepted spawn proposals' count and respawn onto the map as one undo step, after an automatic checkpoint, save, and open the changes review; Install puts them on the server, checkpoint_restore takes them back.
